children: By Caroline Valetkevitch
US Treasury yields inched higher in choppy trading on Thursday as recent hawkish comments from Federal Reserve officials kept focus on the rate hike outlook, while gains in the Nasdaq
pressured bond prices.
US stocks were mixed in late-morning trading although the Nasdaq was higher amid enthusiasm over Anthropic's market debut.
Traders have been factoring in more rate hikes in the coming months. Yields jumped last week after data showed consumer prices rose faster than expected in October.

J.P. Morgan said on Thursday it expects the Fed to deliver quarter-point rate hikes in January and March next year, on top of a previously forecast December increase, as sticky inflation keeps the need for further tightening in play.

"The Federal Reserve and the potential for future rate hikes, that seems to be front and center in investors' minds. When you have the participants consistently telling the same story, it's very easy for investors to keep trading on that story," said Jim Barnes, director of fixed income at Bryn Mawr Trust.
Also, he said, "we've  had some appreciation back in the stock market. You have that risk on tone and... you see Treasuries just basically taking the risk off direction."

The Fed is widely expected to raise interest rates in December after leaving rates unchanged in October. It hiked rates in September for the first time in three years in an effort to combat inflation.

Fed funds futures traders on Thursday were pricing in a 95% chance of a 25-basis-point hike at the US central bank's December 8-9 meeting, according to the CME Group's FedWatch Tool, and a 5% chance of a 50-basis-point hike.
Among recent hawkish comments, Fed Governor Christopher Waller said on CNBC on Wednesday that the central bank needs to get more aggressive in its response to inflation.
The Anthropic IPO could raise sentiment on the AI trade following last week's big drop in AI leader Nvidia
. Nvidia, whose CEO Jensen Huang stepped down last week following revelations about extramarital affairs, had helped drive the four-year-old US bull market.
Yields trimmed their gain early after economic data showed the number of Americans filing new claims for unemployment benefits increased slightly last week.
The yield on the benchmark US 10-year Treasury note
was up 0.2 basis points at 5.068%. The yield on the 30-year bond (US30YT=RR) was up 0.1 basis points at 5.414%.

A closely watched part of the US Treasury yield curve measuring the gap between yields on two- and 10-year Treasury notes (US2US10=TWEB), seen as an indicator of economic expectations, was at a positive 25.5 basis points.
The 2-year (US2YT=RR) US Treasury yield, which typically moves in step with interest rate expectations for the Fed, rose 1.1 basis points to 4.811%.
The breakeven rate on 5-year US Treasury Inflation-Protected Securities (TIPS) (US5YTIP=TWEB) was last at 2.233% after closing at 2.231% on Wednesday.
The 10-year TIPS breakeven rate (US10YTIP=TWEB) was last at 2.189%, indicating the market sees inflation averaging about 2.2% a year for the next decade.
